label: Person
name: Anselm of Lucca
summary:
Anselm of Lucca (c. 1020-1086) was a pivotal figure in the Investiture Controversy, a complex web of power struggles between the Holy Roman Empire and the Catholic Church during the tumultuous years of central Italy's medieval politics.

Born Anselm of Baggio, he rose through the ranks to become bishop of Lucca at a relatively young age, succeeding his uncle Anselm who had earlier been elected Pope Alexander II. This dual connection underscores the intricate family dynamics that often characterized the high clergy during this period.

Anselm's involvement in the Investiture Controversy reflects the deeply entwined nature of politics and religion in medieval Italy. His diplomatic efforts to mediate between Emperor Henry IV and his mother, Matilda, countess of Tuscany, demonstrate the personal costs and compromises that often accompanied the pursuit of power in this era.

As a result of his actions, Anselm's legacy is tied to the tumultuous period of Investiture Controversy, which shaped the course of medieval European history. His influence can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Holy Roman Empire and the strengthening of papal authority during the High Middle Ages.

"The faithful who live according to God's will are the ones that truly live." - Pope Alexander II, Anselm's nephew and predecessor as bishop of Lucca
